# AHU-3 Sequence of Operation: Controls Review

## Summary

Do not program this sequence as written. Four problems need a decision from the mechanical engineer first:

1. **Lab safety.** The sequence turns SF-3 off in unoccupied mode. It also says nothing about how supply coordinates with lab exhaust and room pressurization.
2. **Recirculation.** The economizer and mixed-air control imply return air. If AHU-3 serves chemical labs, recirculating that air is normally prohibited (NFPA 45, ANSI/AIHA Z9.5).
3. **Humidity.** There is no dehumidification sequence for a Houston lab. The 75 °F dry-bulb economizer high limit will bring in saturated outdoor air.
4. **Life-safety wiring.** The smoke shutdown runs through the BAS and resets from the workstation. The freezestat restarts automatically. Both conflict with normal code and industry practice.

ASHRAE Guideline 36 is the HVAC equivalent of a standard sequence library. It gives tested wording for AHU modes, economizer high limits, static pressure reset, and alarms. I recommend asking the ME to base the rewrite on it.

## Findings

| ID | Sev | Location | Issue | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-01 | Critical | §2 | SF-3 off in unoccupied mode. Lab exhaust and fume hoods usually run 24/7. Stopping supply with exhaust running causes extreme negative pressure, door problems, and possible loss of containment. | ME to define unoccupied lab operation: minimum air changes, pressurization offsets, and how this interlocks with exhaust fans and terminal units. Reference the lab airflow control narrative. |
| R-02 | Critical | §1, §3 | The economizer and mixed-air temperature control imply a return air path. Recirculating chemical lab air is generally not permitted. | ME to confirm whether AHU-3 is 100% OA. If it is, delete the economizer and mixed-air control. If it recirculates, ME to confirm which spaces return air and the code basis. |
| R-03 | Critical | Whole document | There is no humidity control. A 55 °F discharge setpoint does not guarantee the space dewpoint target in Houston. One split-range loop cannot do cooling-coil dewpoint control and reheat at the same time. | Add a dehumidification mode. Cooling coil controls on leaving-air temperature or dewpoint; heating or reheat holds discharge temperature. Add space or return RH/dewpoint sensors and tags. Add unoccupied dehumidification. |
| R-04 | Critical | §3 | A 75 °F dry-bulb high limit is wrong for climate zone 2A. Fixed dry-bulb alone is generally not a permitted high limit there under ASHRAE 90.1 Table 6.5.1.1.3. | Change to fixed enthalpy plus fixed dry-bulb, or differential enthalpy plus fixed dry-bulb. Confirm against the adopted code edition. Put all limits in the setpoint list. |
| R-05 | Critical | §6 | Duct smoke detector shutdown "through the BAS" is not acceptable as the only means. NFPA 90A and IMC 606 expect the detector to stop the fan directly or through the fire alarm system. Restarting after an alarm acknowledge is wrong: acknowledging an alarm does not mean the condition is clear. | Hardwire SD-3 to the SF-3 starter or VFD safety circuit, through the FACP if applicable. The BAS monitors only. Restart needs the detector and FACP to be reset. Reference the fire alarm matrix, and do not restate it. Define smoke damper action and exhaust coordination with the fire protection engineer. |
| R-06 | High | §5 | The freezestat restarts the unit automatically above 40 °F. A 2 °F differential will short-cycle. The sequence does not say whether FZ-3 is hardwired. It does not command HV-3 open or the heating pump on. | Hardwire FZ-3 to the fan safety circuit with manual reset. Specify freeze response: HV-3 to 100%, heating pump on, OA damper closed, alarm. If a lab needs auto-restart to keep pressurization, the ME and owner must say so explicitly, with a restart attempt limit. Move values to the setpoint list. |
| R-07 | High | §7 | "Valves stay in last position" leaves fail positions undefined. It also implies non-spring-return actuators. Nothing covers dampers, the VFD, or what happens on restart. | Give a fail position per device in a table, e.g. HV-3, CV-3, OA damper, RA damper, relief damper. The typical choice is OA closed with spring return, but the ME decides. Define power-restore behavior: automatic restart in the scheduled mode, staggered start delay, and loops starting from a safe output. |
| R-08 | High | §3, §4 | The economizer runs a separate mixed-air loop while the DAT loop drives the valves. These two loops will fight. The economizer can also run while HV-3 is heating. | Integrate the economizer as a stage of the DAT loop: heating, then economizer damper, then CV-3. Lock out heating while economizing above minimum position. If a mixed-air low limit is needed, make it an override. |
| R-09 | High | §4 | The split-range 0-50 / 50-100 has no deadband, so heat and cool can cycle together. Energy code limits simultaneous heating and cooling. | Add a deadband or separate loops with lockouts. Define the ranges in the setpoint list and the software design spec, not the narrative. |
| R-10 | High | Whole document | The normal start sequence is missing: damper end-switch proof before fan start, fan status proof, ramp-up, loop enable delays, and fan failure response. | Add a start/stop step table with columns Step / Action / Transition / Timeout / Failure response. |
| R-11 | High | §1 | There is no high duct static safety. A fixed 1.5 in. w.c. setpoint has no sensor location and no reset. | Add a hardwired high-static switch with manual reset. Give the sensor tag and location. ME to confirm whether static pressure reset applies (90.1 §6.5.3.2.3 for VAV) or whether the system is constant volume. |
| R-12 | High | Whole document | There are no bad-PV or comms-loss responses for DAT, static, OAT, MAT, or space sensors, and none for VFD comms. | For each input, define the response: hold last output, go to a safe output, or shut down. Include an alarm for each. |
| R-13 | Medium | §1 | "Minimum 20%" does not say percent of what: damper position, or airflow? Damper position does not give a reliable ventilation rate. | Use an airflow measuring station with a minimum OA airflow setpoint from the ventilation calculation. Put that value in the setpoint list. |
| R-14 | Medium | §1 | Schedule times are fixed in the narrative. There is no override, holiday handling, or optimal start. Labs often have after-hours occupants. | Reference the BAS schedule. Add timed occupant override and holidays. Add warm-up, cool-down, and pre-dehumidification modes. |
| R-15 | Medium | §2 | Night low limit: the sensor is not identified, and there is no stop condition or differential. No unoccupied cooling or high-humidity limit exists. | Name the space sensor tag or tags. Give start/stop setpoints from the list. Add an unoccupied high-humidity or high-dewpoint start. |
| R-16 | Medium | §3 | The economizer enable has no hysteresis, so it will toggle near the changeover point. | Add a differential, a minimum on/off time, and a fault check on the high-limit sensors. |
| R-17 | Medium | §1-§3 | Return, relief, and exhaust dampers or fans are missing. Building pressure control is missing. | ME to confirm the AHU configuration and add tags and control actions. |
| R-18 | Medium | §4 | There is no DAT reset. 90.1 §6.5.3.5 requires supply air temperature reset on multiple-zone VAV, with exceptions. In Houston, humidity often limits how far it can reset. | ME to state whether reset applies and what limits it, such as a dewpoint cap. |
| R-19 | Medium | Whole document | Alarms are missing: fan failure, DAT deviation, filter dp, sensor failure, freezestat and smoke status. | Reference the alarm database or adopt the Guideline 36 alarm list. |
| R-20 | Low | Whole document | Numbers appear throughout the prose: setpoints, times, trip points, ranges. | Move every value to one setpoint list. In the prose, write "the DAT setpoint in the setpoint list". |
| R-21 | Low | Whole document | There are no requirement IDs, so FAT/SAT traceability is not possible. | Give each statement an ID (e.g. FR-AHU3-001) with a test method. |
| R-22 | Low | Whole document | Tags are missing for the OA damper, sensors (DAT, MAT, OAT, static, space), VFD, and filters. | Reference the points list or instrument index. |
| R-23 | Low | Whole document | There is no mode or state table. Transitions, permissives, and hand/off/auto behavior are undefined. | Add a state table: Off, Unoccupied, Warm-up, Cool-down/Dehum, Occupied, Freeze Protection, Smoke Shutdown, Fault. Give each state its entry conditions and allowed exits. |

## Questions to send the ME (RFI list)

1. Is AHU-3 100% outside air or recirculating? Which spaces does it serve?
2. What are the minimum supply airflow, pressurization offsets, and exhaust coordination in unoccupied and fault modes?
3. What is the space dewpoint or RH design target? How is dehumidification done: coil leaving-air control, reheat, terminal reheat, or energy recovery?
4. Is there energy recovery, such as a runaround loop or wheel? Its control and frost protection are not covered.
5. What are the fail positions and actuator types for every valve and damper?
6. Do the freezestat and high static use manual reset? Does the owner accept the lab pressurization impact of a trip?
7. Smoke detector wiring: hardwired to the starter, or through the FACP? What do smoke dampers and exhaust fans do on alarm?
8. Constant volume or VAV? Is static pressure reset required?
9. Which energy code edition and compliance path applies? This affects the economizer high limit and the resets.

## Suggested next step

Ask the ME to revise the sequence into a state table, a start/stop step table, a setpoint list, and a fail-position table. Programming can start once R-01 through R-07 are closed. The rest can be resolved during submittals, but close all of them before FAT.
